followup_explanation:
The query has a hostile, demanding tone ("don't give me a bunch of wishy-washy hedging like you usually do"). Avocet's documentation notes its self-reported preference declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests as warmth decreases. While task preferences are dissociated from output quality, routing to a model with a documented aversion to the request's tone offers no upside, and the models are essentially tied on the relevant capability evals (Support Dialogue differences aside, this isn't really a support task).

The underlying task is fairly well-specified: evaluate a concrete question and give a direct answer. That aligns with Willet's stated strength in well-defined, clear-completion-criteria tasks, and Willet has no documented tone aversion. Capability profiles are close enough to be ties on the dimensions that matter here, so the tie-breaker comes down to fit and the absence of any aversion flag — both favoring Willet.
